meta.title: Somali A1 Beginner
meta.subtitle: 400 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Somali → English (see the Somali, recall the meaning) and English → Somali (see an English meaning, recall the Somali). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 400 words for a beginner, aligned to A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases aimed at the satisfaction of needs of a concrete type' — a learner here is able to introduce themselves and others, to ask and answer questions about personal details such as where they live, people they know and things they have, and to interact in a simple way provided the other person talks slowly and clearly and is prepared to help. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Somali, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 275 of the 400 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — greetings and politeness, the pronouns, question and joining words, numbers, people and the family, the body and feeling ill, time and the days of the week, food and drink, money and shopping, the home and clothes, the town and getting about, the weather, colours, animals, school and work, the everyday verbs, describing things, and the little words of place and manner every sentence is built out of — and the other 125 are the commonest remaining words of the Somali Wikipedia (its articles of 150 words or more), each counted over its forms, since Somali writes the article and the endings onto the word (buugga 'the book', cunay 'ate'). The corpus is encyclopaedic, which shows in the fill (places, history, government), and the cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words met most often come first. THE SOURCES ARE THIN: English Wiktionary has about a thousand Somali words and lacks some of the commonest (tag 'go', lacag 'money', hadda 'now'), so 87 of the 400 are glossed by Folio itself with the standard meaning a course or dictionary gives. Words are written in the ordinary Somali spelling, which marks no tone; under 92 of them is the accented spelling English Wiktionary gives (nín 'man', gabádh 'girl'), the accent marking the high tone that tells, for instance, a masculine noun from a feminine one. Folio's own glosses carry none, since an accent from memory would be a claim with no source. A noun's gender is in its label and its plural is given with the plural's own gender, which is often the other one (wiil 'boy' is masculine, wiilal 'boys' feminine). The Alphabet deck, first in this collection, teaches the letters, among them c, x, q, dh and the long vowels. Example sentences are few: 40 of the 400 words have one, from Wiktionary's usage examples and from Tatoeba, which holds about 125 Somali sentences with a translation; none is invented. There is no speaker button: few devices have a Somali voice, and one without it would read the word in another language's sounds. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, accents, genders and plurals: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0), and Folio's own glosses for the words it lacks. Frequency: the Somali Wikipedia, articles of the 2026-11-01 dump (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
